\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{کھنڈر} (khanḍar)}{کھنڈر (khanḍar)}]{\ur{کھنڈر} (khanḍar) — ruins}

\label{lesson:UR-C314-khandar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a sacrifice, then the Urdu for to entrust.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{کھنڈر}}
\textbf{\ur{کھنڈر}} — \emph{khanḍar} — \textquotedblleft{}ruins\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{پہاڑی} \ur{پر} \ur{ایک} \ur{پرانا} \ur{کھنڈر} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pahāṛī par ek purānā khanḍar hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There are old ruins on the hill.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{کھنڈر}} (\emph{khanḍar}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{khaṇḍhar}, \textquotedblleft{}a dilapidated building, ruins\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{*khaṇḍaghara}, a broken house, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 3794).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khanḍar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khanḍar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pahāṛī par ek purānā khanḍar hai.} — There are old ruins on the hill.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a sacrifice, then the Urdu for to entrust, then say \emph{khanḍar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{کھنڈر} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Ruins\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{کھودنا} (khodnā)}{کھودنا (khodnā)}]{\ur{کھودنا} (khodnā) — to dig}

\label{lesson:UR-C314-khodna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to entrust, then the Urdu for ruins.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{کھودنا}}
\textbf{\ur{کھودنا}} — \emph{khodnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to dig\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{مزدوروں} \ur{نے} \ur{کھنڈر} \ur{میں} \ur{زمین} \ur{کھودی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mazdūroṅ ne khanḍar meṅ zamīn khodī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The labourers dug the ground in the ruins.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{زمین} \ur{کھودی}, \emph{us ne zamīn khodī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{کھودنا}} (\emph{khodnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{khodnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to dig, to carve\textquotedblright{}, under a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 3934).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khodnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khodnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mazdūroṅ ne khanḍar meṅ zamīn khodī.} — The labourers dug the ground in the ruins.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to entrust, then the Urdu for ruins, then say \emph{khodnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{کھودنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To dig\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{مجسمہ} (mujassamā)}{مجسمہ (mujassamā)}]{\ur{مجسمہ} (mujassamā) — a statue}

\label{lesson:UR-C314-mujassama}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for ruins, then the Urdu for to dig.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{مجسمہ}}
\textbf{\ur{مجسمہ}} — \emph{mujassamā} — \textquotedblleft{}a statue\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{انہیں} \ur{ایک} \ur{پرانا} \ur{مجسمہ} \ur{ملا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{unheṅ ek purānā mujassamā milā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
They found an old statue.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{مجسمہ}} (\emph{mujassamā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{mujassam}, \textquotedblleft{}given a body, made solid\textquotedblright{}: a figure in stone or metal.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{کتبہ} (katbā)}{کتبہ (katbā)}]{\ur{کتبہ} (katbā) — an inscription}

\label{lesson:UR-C314-katba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to dig, then the Urdu for a statue.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{کتبہ}}
\textbf{\ur{کتبہ}} — \emph{katbā} — \textquotedblleft{}an inscription\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{پتھر} \ur{پر} \ur{ایک} \ur{کتبہ} \ur{تھا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{patthar par ek katbā thā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There was an inscription on the stone.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{کتبہ}} (\emph{katbā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{katba}, \textquotedblleft{}a piece of writing\textquotedblright{}. It is writing cut into stone or metal.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{katbā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{katbā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{patthar par ek katbā thā.} — There was an inscription on the stone.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to dig, then the Urdu for a statue, then say \emph{katbā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{آثار} (āsār)}{آثار (āsār)}]{\ur{آثار} (āsār) — ancient remains; traces}

\label{lesson:UR-C314-asar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a statue, then the Urdu for an inscription.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{آثار}}
\textbf{\ur{آثار}} — \emph{āsār} — \textquotedblleft{}ancient remains; traces\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{یہاں} \ur{پرانے} \ur{شہر} \ur{کے} \ur{آثار} \ur{ہیں۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yahāṅ purāne shahr ke āsār haiṅ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Here are the remains of an old city.
\end{quote}

Masculine, used in the plural.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{آثار}} (\emph{āsār}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{āthār}, \textquotedblleft{}traces\textquotedblright{}, the plural of the word behind \textbf{\ur{اثر}}. It takes a plural verb: \textbf{\ur{آثار} \ur{ہیں}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āsār}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āsār}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yahāṅ purāne shahr ke āsār haiṅ.} — Here are the remains of an old city.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a statue, then the Urdu for an inscription, then say \emph{āsār} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
